resources.string: Scanning this phone. Nothing is being changed.

This app looks for anything on this phone that could watch you: hidden apps, apps with deep control, apps holding microphone, camera or location access they do not need, apps that run constantly, and where apps send data. It only reads. It never installs, removes or changes anything.
Usage access (optional): lets the app see which apps ran in the background this week. Android asks you on a Settings screen. Without it the Persistence check is reported as not checked.

Local network monitor (coming in a later version): a local VPN that watches which names apps look up. Android asks you with a system dialog. It stops when the scan ends and never redirects or stores your traffic.
Every report lists exactly what the scan touched.
One tap scans the phone and writes a plain language report: a verdict, three lists, and the single most important thing to do next.
Usage access: not granted. The Persistence check will be reported as not checked.
The Network check is not part of this version yet. The report says so.
